newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia govt warns on inflation complacency.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia govt warns on inflation complacency.

text.p: Australian Industrial Relations Minister Peter Reith on Monday warned against complacency on inflation and wages growth, despite recent encouraging signs.

"The latest inflation and average weekly earnings figures from the bureau of statistics are certainly encouraging and should be welcomed, although there remain no grounds for complacency on the inflation and wages front," Reith said.
"In particular, the enterprise bargaining data are yet to show any substantive sign of easing in wage outcomes from agreements," he said in a speech.
Official figures on enterprise bargaining -- private wage deals between workers and employers -- show an annual increase of 6.5 percent for the March quarter. New figures are expected next week.
Australia's consumer price index inflation was 2.1 percent in the September quarter.
Treasurer Peter Costello said last week official interest rates could be cut further if wages growth and inflation could be restrained.
The Reserve Bank cut official rates to 6.5 percent from 7.0 percent last week, the second cut since another 0.5 percentage point reduction in July.

"The overriding objectives of the government's economic policy are to improve Australia's living standards and to reduce Australia's totally unacceptable level of unemployment, particularly youth unemployment, which currently stands at an appalling 28 percent," Reith said in the speech prepared for delivery at the conference.
The speech, delivered later, made no reference to inflation or wages.
